subject: Science
title: Growing a seed
objectives: Children will plant a seed and water it.
Children will notice and talk about changes as the seed grows.
content: Looking at seeds, planting a bean seed, and watering and waiting while it grows.
teachingActivities: Use large bean seeds that are easy to handle; plant in clear cups so children can see roots; keep a growth chart with pictures; talk about waiting; never let children eat seeds.
learnerActivities: Plant a seed, water it and notice and talk about changes as it grows.
resources: Pictures of seed, root and shoot
assessment: Observe whether each child plants a seed with support and says grow or points to change.

lessons.title: Looking at seeds
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will look at seeds and say that plants grow from seeds.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name plants and plant parts and know that plants are alive and grow.
resources: A picture of a bean plant
lessons.starter: Hold up a large bean seed and say "This is a seed. A plant is asleep inside."
teacherActivities: Show different seeds and let children touch them gently.
Look at a seed with a magnifying glass.
Show a picture of a bean plant growing from a seed.
Say "Seeds need water and soil to grow."
learnerActivities: Children touch the seeds and say seed.
Children look closely and point.
Children look and say plant.
Children say water and soil.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show different seeds and let children touch them gently. Children: Children touch the seeds and say seed.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at a seed with a magnifying glass. Children: Children look closely and point.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a picture of a bean plant growing from a seed. Children: Children look and say plant.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Seeds need water and soil to grow." Children: Children say water and soil.

practical.title: Seed tray
steps: Put large seeds on a tray.
Look at them with a magnifying glass.
Sort them by size or colour.
practical.safety: Use only large seeds that cannot be swallowed and supervise closely. Remind children not to put seeds in their mouths or noses.

differentiation.support: Hold a seed together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two seeds that look different.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Looks at seeds and says seed
Says that a plant grows from a seed
lessons.conclusion: Put the seeds in a box and say "Tomorrow we plant them."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at seeds in fruit such as an orange or a pawpaw with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "look at seeds and say that plants grow from seeds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: A little seed, a little seed, grows into a plant.

lessons.title: Planting a seed
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will plant a bean seed in a cup of soil.
successCriteria: Plants a seed and covers it
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name plants and plant parts and know that plants are alive and grow.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we plant a seed. First soil, then the seed, then more soil." Show the three steps.
teacherActivities: Show how to fill a cup with soil with a spoon.
Show how to push a seed into the soil with a finger.
Cover the seed with soil and write the child’s name on the cup.
Water the soil gently with a watering can.
learnerActivities: Children fill their cups with soil.
Child pushes a seed in.
Child pats the soil and sees their name.
Child waters their cup.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to fill a cup with soil with a spoon. Children: Children fill their cups with soil.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to push a seed into the soil with a finger. Children: Child pushes a seed in.
Step 3. Teacher: Cover the seed with soil and write the child’s name on the cup. Children: Child pats the soil and sees their name.
Step 4. Teacher: Water the soil gently with a watering can. Children: Child waters their cup.

practical.title: Plant a seed
steps: Put soil in a clear cup.
Plant a bean seed and cover it.
Water gently and put the cup in the sun.
practical.safety: Use clean soil and wash hands after planting. Keep seeds out of mouths. Wipe spilled water.

differentiation.support: Plant the seed together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to plant two seeds and say which one will grow first.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we put in the cup first?

lessons.conclusion: Put the cups in a sunny place and say "Grow, seed, grow."
lessons.homeConnection: Plant a seed at home with your child in a small pot.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "plant a bean seed in a cup of soil" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Watering and waiting
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will water their seeds and notice changes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name plants and plant parts and know that plants are alive and grow.
resources: Pictures of a seed, root and shoot
lessons.starter: Look at the cups together and say "Our seeds are asleep. Let us give them a drink."
teacherActivities: Water each cup gently and say "Drink, seed."
Look at the soil and ask "Has anything changed?"
Show the growth chart and talk about waiting.
Draw or stick a picture on the chart for today.
learnerActivities: Children water their cups.
Child looks and says yes or no.
Children listen and look.
Child adds a picture to the chart.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Water each cup gently and say "Drink, seed." Children: Children water their cups.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at the soil and ask "Has anything changed?" Children: Child looks and says yes or no.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the growth chart and talk about waiting. Children: Children listen and look.
Step 4. Teacher: Draw or stick a picture on the chart for today. Children: Child adds a picture to the chart.

practical.title: Water the seeds
steps: Look closely and record on the chart.
practical.safety: Do not overwater; one small splash is enough. Keep the floor dry and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Water together and point to the soil.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess when the seed will grow.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Has the seed grown?
questions.expected: Not yet or yes, with a shoot.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cups back and say "Wait for the seed."
lessons.homeConnection: Water a plant at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "water their seeds and notice changes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Seeds in cotton wool
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will plant a seed in cotton wool and watch the root and shoot appear.
successCriteria: Plants a seed in damp cotton wool
Looks at the roots through the cup
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name plants and plant parts and know that plants are alive and grow.
resources: A picture of a root and a shoot
lessons.starter: Show a clear cup and say "We can see the seed grow if we plant it in cotton wool."
teacherActivities: Put damp cotton wool in the cup and push a seed against the glass.
Put the cup on a sunny windowsill.
Look each day for a root going down and a shoot going up.
Show the picture of a root and a shoot.
learnerActivities: Child pushes the seed against the cup.
Child places the cup in a sunny spot.
Child looks and points to the root.
Child matches the picture to the seed.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put damp cotton wool in the cup and push a seed against the glass. Children: Child pushes the seed against the cup.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the cup on a sunny windowsill. Children: Child places the cup in a sunny spot.
Step 3. Teacher: Look each day for a root going down and a shoot going up. Children: Child looks and points to the root.
Step 4. Teacher: Show the picture of a root and a shoot. Children: Child matches the picture to the seed.

practical.title: See it grow
steps: Put damp cotton wool in a clear cup.
Push a seed against the glass.
Look each day for roots and shoots.
practical.safety: Keep the cups on a tray to catch spills and wash hands after touching. Do not let children eat cotton wool or seeds.

differentiation.support: Hold the cup together and look closely.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw the seed each day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which way does the root grow?
Which way does the shoot grow?

expectedOutcomes: Plants a seed in cotton wool
Notices root and shoot with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cups on the windowsill and say "We will watch each day."
lessons.homeConnection: Grow a bean seed in damp cotton wool at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "plant a seed in cotton wool and watch the root and shoot appear" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 seeds check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child plants and cares for a seed.
successCriteria: Says grow or points to change
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name plants and plant parts and know that plants are alive and grow.
lessons.starter: Look at the cups and sing the seed song.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: looking at seeds, watering and the growth chart.
At each station ask "What does the seed need?" and "What has changed?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children wash hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: looking at seeds, watering and the growth chart. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What does the seed need?" and "What has changed?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Seed stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Use large seeds only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain how to plant a seed.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: plants a seed; waters gently; notices changes; says what a seed needs.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and wave goodbye to the seeds.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep watching plants grow at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child plants and cares for a seed" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
